The two-way out-of-phase divider/combiner shows simulated return loss better than 15dB, amplitude imbalance and phase imbalance approximately 0.1dB and 1°, over 172-240GHz band. The four-way out-of-phase divider/combiner shows return loss, amplitude imbalance and phase imbalance better than 15dB, 0.1dB and 0.8°, respectively, over 185-233GHz band.

articleTitle: A 77 GHz Series-fed Leaky-Wave Antenna for Automotive Radar System
abstract: A <tex>$1.5\mathbf{mm}\times 28\mathbf{mm}$</tex> patch leaky-wave antenna (P-LWA) with a high gain and a large beamwidth in H-plane is proposed for 77GHz automotive radars. Four slots were etched on the driven patch to satisfy the beamwidth requirement in H-plane, which acts as the array element. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna can achieve an impedance bandwidth of 1.3% (76-77GHz) and a maximum realized gain of 15.23dBi. Besides, the proposed antenna can offere an HPBW greater than 118.07° in the H-plane.

articleTitle: Wideband Wide-angle Scanning Millimeter-Wave Phased Array Antenna Based on Magneto-electric Dipole
abstract: In this manuscript, a wide-beam wideband magneto-electric (ME) dipole is proposed. The band of the antenna can cover 24.25 to 29.5GHz (19.5%), and after loading the stepped ground, the antenna has a beamwidth of over 110° in the E-plane. Then, the newly designed element is placed with a small distance of 4.5mm (about 0.4AO at 27GHz) for implementing 4x4 wide-angle scanning phased array. Several II-shaped decoupling structures are placed between adjacent elements along the E-plane direction to reduce coupling and therefore improve active S-parameters. The results show that the array can cover the band of 24.25 to 29.5GHz (19.5%), and has a large scanned area from -57° to 56° with a gain drop below 3dB, while all the port isolation is higher than 20dB, and all the active S-parameter is lower than -10dB.

articleTitle: A Doubler Chain with 13-dBm Output Power for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application
abstract: In this paper, a doubler chain with 13-dBm output power and 35-dBc fundamental rejection is proposed for 5G millimeter-wave application. A bandpass structure is introduced to achieve out-of-band rejection while obtaining a good matching between the doubler and the post-driver. Pre- and post-drivers are deployed in the doubler chain to reduce the power requirement of the local oscillator and obtain high output power at the second harmonic band. The test chip was fabricated in a 0.13-µm SiGe BiCMOS technology with a core size of 0.4 mm<sup>2</sup>. Measurements show that the doubler chain produces up to 13-dBm out-put power at an input power of 2 dBm. In the frequency band of 28–36 GHz, the fundamental rejection is better than 35 dBc and the third-harmonic rejection is better than 28 dBc.

articleTitle: A Compact Common-Aperture S/Ka-band Dual Circularly Polarized Feed for Satellite Applications
abstract: Driven by the application requirements of multi-band systems, multi-band common-aperture antenna has always been a research focus. This paper presents a compact dual-band dual circularly polarized feed based the Choke horn and circular dipole. This feed operating at S-band (2.2GHz-2.4GHz) and Ka-band (18.2GHz-21.2GHz) has almost identical -10dB radiation pattern. When illuminating the parabolic reflector antenna with its aperture of 1.8m and ratio of focal length to diameter of 0.375, the reflector antenna has the gain of 30dB/50dB and the aperture efficiency of 55%/69% at 2.3GHz/20.2GHz. The simulation results show that this presented dual-band dual circularly polarized feed can be a good candidate for satellite, remote sensing and other applications.

articleTitle: ISRNM: A Highly Integrated Module Design for Intersatellite Telemetry & Telecommand and Navigation
abstract: This paper proposed a highly integrated, low-power, multi-functional prototype design of the on board intersatellite Telemetry & Telecommand and navigation module, which includes 3 × 2 MIMO channels to accomplish functions of measurement and control communication, interplanetary networking and BeiDou navigation and communication. A USB compatible with spread spectrum system was supported in this module and the communication data rate of the intersatellite links can reach up to 2MBps. The module was interfaced with the on-board computer through the CAN bus, SRIO communication interface for Telemetry & Telecommand up/down links, on-board health monitoring, high-speed data communication.

articleTitle: A Double Fold Multibeam Antenna for 5G Applications
abstract: In this paper, a double-folded Butler matrix multi-beam antenna based on SIW structure is proposed. The new <tex>$7\times 8$</tex> BM combines two intermediate input ports of the traditional <tex>$8\times 8$</tex> Butler matrix into one port, which provides output signals in the same phase so that the antenna can generate a beam of line-of-sight light. BM is folded twice to form three layers to make the BM size more compact. The measured results show that the maximum gain of this antenna is 17.3dBi within 29.5~30.5 GHz. The antenna is capable of generating 7 beams, including a boresight beam, which can scan in the range of -58°to 58°. It has obvious practical value in 5G.

articleTitle: A Novel Orbital Angular Momentum(OAM) Waves Generator based on Fabry-Perot Resonant Cavity
abstract: A novel orbital angular momentum(OAM) electromagnetic generator based on Fabry-Perot(FP) resonant cavity is proposed in this work. The proposed OAM waves generator is consisted of a feed antenna, and a partially reflective surface(PRS) loaded with a three-dimensional(3D) spiral phase plate. The 3D spiral phase plate is set on the top side of PRS to provide different phases for plane waves with different directions to generate OAM electromagnetic waves. The most important feature of the proposed OAM waves generator is high gain, smaller divergence angle and simple feeding source, without external complex feed network for array of OAM antenna. Then we analyze and discuss the simulated results to prove the feasibility of generating OAM waves.

articleTitle: A Ka-band High Gain Wideband Low Noise Amplifier in $.18-\mu \mathrm{m}\ \text{SiGe}$ BiCMOS
abstract: This paper presents a design approach for Ka-band low noise amplifier (LNA) with both high gain and wide bandwidth. With a five-stage cascode structure, emitter degeneration is used in the first stage to implement the simultaneous power and noise matching and positive-feedback network is adopted to enhance the gain in the next four stages. By using stagger tuning technique, wide bandwidth can be achieved. For demonstration, a Ka-band LNA is designed and fabricated in a 0.18 <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}\ \mathbf{SiGe}$</tex> BiCMOS process. It achieves a 3-dB bandwidth from 31.6 GHz to 38.2 GHz with a maximum gain of 42.9 dB. The circuit operates from a 2.5 V supply with a DC power consumption of 60 mW.

articleTitle: Filtering Antenna Array based to Graphene-Assembled Films for 5G Applications
abstract: <tex>$A$</tex> filtering antenna array based on graphene assembled film (GAF) operating in 3.5 GHz is presented in this paper. The GAF has a conductivity of 10<sup>6</sup> S/m and a thickness of 25 μm with excellent ductility and flexibility. Split-Ring Resonator (SRR) is loaded on side of the feeder to provide filtering characteristics for the upper band of the GAF antenna. Meanwhile, a H-shaped slot is etched the ground below the feeder to suppress the lower band. The gain of the proposed 1 × 2 GAF antenna array can arrive at 5.36 dBi at the working frequency. In addition, the - 10dB impedance bandwidth of GAF antenna array covers the range of 3.45 GHz-3.6 GHz with the good sideband suppression of 20dB. All the results show that GAF filtering antenna array has the important application potential for 5G mobile communications.

articleTitle: Near Field Shaping with Space-Time-Coding Digital Metasurface
abstract: In recent years, space-time-coding digital metasurface (STCM) has been widely studied for its ability of simultaneously manipulating wavefronts and spectrums of the electromagnetic (EM) wave. However, researchers usually focus on the far-field characteristics of the EM waves reflected from the STCM, such as the scattering pattern for beam shaping. Here, we expand our scope to the near field manipulating with STCM. Actually, in many scenarios, STCM can be a good candidate for shaping near field. For example, for the synthesis of plane wave in the compact antenna test range (CA TR), the parabolic reflector can be replaced by the low-cost, light-weight STCM. Moreover, as STCMs can control the EM wavefronts at both fundamental and harmonic frequencies, it can generate near field plane waves along arbitrary directions at multiple frequencies. In this article, we will illustrate the mechanism of linear and nonlinear near field shaping with STCM. Then, we will consider the synthesis of quasi-plane wave in the near field for the 1<sup>st</sup> order harmonic.

articleTitle: The Design of a 20 GHz Switch Network Based on Microwave Multi-Layer Printing Technology
abstract: In this paper, a 20 GHz switch network based on microwave multi-layer printing technology is presented. Due to the excellent high-integration characteristic, multi-layer printing technology is widely used in microwave circuit designs. A 3D electromagnetic field simulation software and PCB circuit co-design method is utilized for a 20 GHz switch network design. Measured results show that the insertion loss of each channel in the 1-to-8 switch is 10 dB. The isolation between two adjacent channels is 25.7 dB.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Transmission Metasurface for Linear Polarization Conversion and Beam Control
abstract: In this paper, a multi-layer transmission metasurface for high efficiency linear polarization (LP) conversion and beam control is proposed. The metasurface unit cell is composed of three layers of metal and two layers of dielectric. The top and bottom metal layers are orthogonal grids while the middle metal layer is C-shaped split ring. By altering the opening angle of C-shaped metal split ring, phase-gradient metasurface is proposed. Simulation results have proved that polarization conversion ratio (PCR) is above 90% and the beam of electromagnetic wave (EMW) can be refracted 30° at 10GHz, which is a good validation of the generalized Snell's law.

articleTitle: A Double-Layer Wideband Transmitarray Antenna with Compensation Elements
abstract: A double-layer wideband transmitarray antenna with small compensation elements is proposed. The double-layer transmitarray antenna consists of 441 standard elements and 128 small elements. Standard elements have two freedom degrees, which can achieve a 360° phase shift range. And small elements placed at the intersection of the four standard elements is able to generate an approximate 90° phase shift range. The simulation results show that the phase shift curve of the small unit is very flat with wide bandwidth. Therefore, the addition of small elements can not only increase the gain but also increase the bandwidth. The array is designed, manufactured and testing. The experimental data is in good agreement with the simulation. The proposed transmitarray achieves a gain of 29.5 dB at 34 GHz, with an aperture efficiency of 41% and 1dB gain bandwidth of 10.3% (32.1GHz-35.6GHz). The small elements can also be added to other similar lens antenna to enhance the gain and bandwidth.

articleTitle: Symmetrical Four-Port Reflectionless Network And Its Application For Wideband Filter/Diplexer Design
abstract: In this paper, a symmetrical four-port reflectionless network is proposed. Based on the proposed network, two pairs of bandpass filter (BPF) and bandstop filter (BSF) with complementary response are used for circuit implementation. The proposed circuit can not only achieve bandpass/bandstop function between arbitrary two adjacent ports, but also exhibit reflectionless characteristic at all ports. Meanwhile, the BPF consists of two T-junctions with defected ground structure (DGS), while the BSF is composed of stepped-impedance resonator (SIR) and DGS. To verify the mechanisms, an all-port reflectionless filter/diplexer (i.e., four-port circuit) operating at center frequency <tex>$f_{0}$</tex> of 4.34 GHz with 58.0% fractional bandwidth (FBW) is implemented and fabricated. The measured reflectionless range is from 0.01 to 9 GHz with the reflectionless level below 10 dB.

articleTitle: Design of Transmissive Near-Field Focusing Metasurface for Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: In this paper, the transmissive near-field focusing metasurfaces for wireless power transfer are designed. The transmissive unit consists of three dielectric layers and four metal layers. The metal layer adopts a diamond-shaped patch embedded in a rectangular box, and a circular slot is added to the center of the diamond. The transmission coefficient magnitude of the unit can be beyond 0.8. Meanwhile, the phase of the transmission coefficient can cover 360°. A single-focus transmissive metasurface and a dual-focus transmissive metasurface operating at 10 GHz are designed by employing the proposed unit.

articleTitle: A Low Power Sub-GHz PLL with Optimized Class-C Voltage-controlled Oscillator
abstract: A wideband fractional-N phase-lock loop (PLL) is designed for sub-GHz wireless communications. Class-C voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) circuit is optimized with low power consumption, followed by all-digital programmable counter to achieve flexibility in operating frequency. Implemented with a commercial 0.11-μm CMOS process, the proposed PLL has a working range of 680MHz - 998MHz with 2.69m W power consumption, including all the buffers from a 1.5V supply. It occupies a silicon area of 0.12mm<sup>2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of 30–50 GHz Broadband Up-Conversion Mixer Using 65 nm CMOS Technology
abstract: A 30–50 GHz up-conversion mixer is present in this paper using 65nm CMOS technology. The mixer consists of a double balanced Gilbert cell and a resistive feedback amplifier, which is used to increase conversion gain while maintaining a low DC consumption. The Marchand balun is implemented at RF and LO ports to realize the broadband matching and mutual transformation between differential signal and single-ended signal. According to the measurement results, for RF frequencies from 30 GHz to 50 GHz, the mixer achieves a conversion gain of 4.81-2.49 dB at an IF frequencies of 2 GHz. The proposed mixer achieves an output 1dB compression point of -7.16 dBm at 45 GHz. The chip size is only 0.256 mm<sup>2</sup>and the dc consumption is only 12.98mW from a 1.1 V supply.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an S/C Band Tile-Type TR Module
abstract: An ultra-wide band tile-type Transmit/Receive module (T/R module) with the characteristics of high integration, small volume, light-weight is presented in this paper. The proposed T/R module can realize transmit/receive signal amplification, amplitude and phase control. In electrical design, two 2-channels multi-function MMICs (MFC) are applied to provide the amplitude and phase control of RF signal. And it is remarkable that large, the MFC is a three-dimensional (3D) chip which achieved by stacking digital circuits on top of the microwave circuits to increase densities. And 4 RF front modules are applied to realize transmit/receive signal amplification. The designed T/R module provides above 30dB of receive gain with Noise Figure (NF) better than 2.5dB, and up to 40dBm of pulsed power with about 35% of power added efficiency (PAE). In mechanical design, a newly assembly method of 3D vertical interconnection technology in the highly integrated packaging TR module is proposed. Signals transmission between the proposed TR module and the external system are achieved by fuzz-button connectors to form a vertical interconnection structure. The designed 4-channels T/R module is about 38mm38mm*8mm, and the total weight is 30g.

articleTitle: Generation of 1D-Airy Beams Based on Scalar Holographic Metasurface
abstract: The Airy beams have intrigued many researchers because of their unusual characteristics. There are few studies on Airy beams in the microwave field, and the devices currently used to create Airy beams are complex. So, in this paper, a scalar holographic metasurface is proposed to generate a one-dimensional Airy beam, which reduces the complexity of the generation device of the Airy beam. The simulation results at 12 GHz show this paper's proposed method's correctness.

articleTitle: A Self-Biased 210–260 GHz Frequency Tripler Based on Planar Schottky Diodes
abstract: This paper describes the design and demonstration of a hybrid integrated 210~260 GHz self-biased frequency tripler based on planar Schottky diodes. Two Schottky diodes are placed in reversed parallel on the circuit. Then, a self-bias resistor is connected to the circuit to provide a DC bias. The bias voltage is changed by adjusting the resistances, so that the tripler can fit in the best working state. In addition, the current saturation effect is considered in the nonlinear simulation of the circuit to obtain more accurate simulated results. The proposed tripler was fabricated on a 50-um thickness quartz substrate circuit and housed in split waveguide blocks. Measured results show that the tripler exhibits a peak output power of 6.4 dBm at 220 GHz with 20 dBm pumped power and a wide 3 dB bandwidth of 21 % from 210 GHz to 260 GHz with a conversion efficiency above 2.2%.

articleTitle: A Transformed-based Ka-band GaN Low-Noise Amplifier MMIC
abstract: This paper reports the design of a broadband GaN low noise amplifier (LNA) microwave monolithic integrated circuit (MMIC). A novel transformer structure is proposed to implement the gm-boosting as well as bandwidth extension in the LNA. The designed LNA shows >20dB gain, <2dB noise figure (NF) and >14.5dBm output 1dB compression point (OP1dB) within a wide working frequency range from 20 to 41GHz, which fully covers the Ka-band. In addition, the gain and NF fluctuation is less than 2dB and 0.7dB, respectively. The die size of the LNA MMIC is 1.6×1mm<sup>2</sup>. This work verifies the feasibility of the transformer-based LNA design in GaN MMIC platform.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Gradient-based EM Optimization using Neuro-TF Surrogate
abstract: A surrogate model composed of neural networks and transfer functions has been presented to execute efficient electromagnetic (EM) optimization instead of using a coarse model. It is called neuro-transfer function (neuro-TF). This paper introduces the recent advances in neuro-TF methods for electromagnetic optimization, including multifeature-assisted method and adjoint sensitivity-based method. Further speedup in EM optimization is achieved using these neuro-TF surrogate optimization methods.

articleTitle: A 300 GHz SiGe Double-Balanced Passive Third Harmonic Mixer Using PMOS Varactors
abstract: This paper presents a compact 300 GHz double-balanced passive third harmonic mixer in a 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS process. In the 300 GHz band, traditional varactors have a low capacitance ratio, resulting in the poor performance of varactor-based passive mixers. In this paper, we proposed a high capacitance ratio varactor based on PMOS transistors and apply it to the design of a 300 GHz double-balanced passive mixer. The RF output power of the mixer is greatly improved by the proposed varactor. The mixer achieves a simulated maximum output 1dB compression point (OP<inf>1dB</inf>) of 0 dBm and maximum saturation power (P<inf>sat</inf>) of 2.7 dBm at 325 GHz with a LO frequency (f<inf>LO</inf>) of 75 GHz and LO power (P<inf>LO</inf>) of 25 dBm. The conversion gain (CG) is -19 dB with 3 dB bandwidth from 285 to 335 GHz. Benefiting from the double-balanced structure, the IF-to-RF, LO-to-IF, and LO-to-RF isolation performance are better than 42 dBc, 52 dBc, and 40 dBc.

articleTitle: A Feedback-regulated BDS GSMC Access Strategy
abstract: The terminal of BDS GSMC (Global Short Message Communication) are usually covered by several satellites of BDS constellation. When initialing the GSMC services, how to select the most proper satellite in the group of several visible satellites as the access satellite is a challenge. To solve the Insufficient of existing satellite selection strategy with priority of elevation angle that the system is prone to congestion due to neglect of satellite prior knowledge, a shunting satellite selection strategy based on feedback adjustment is proposed. The proposed strategy makes full use of constellation resources through closed-loop feedback. The comparative simulation results of different strategies show that, when the number of users accessing per hour exceeds 250,000, the blocking rate of our method based on feedback adjustment is reduced by more than 2.5% compared with other existing strategies. At the same time, the standard deviation of the selection times of each satellite is reduced about 52 %, which effectively improves the success rate of user access and the utilization rate of satellite resources.

articleTitle: A Compact Filtenna for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
abstract: In this paper, a compact high-selectivity filter antenna (filtenna) for <tex>$5\mathrm{G}$</tex> millimeter wave (mmWave) applications is introduced. It comprises two circular patches, two annular patches and a circular substrate integrated waveguide(SIW) cavity. Through the special slot design of the upper and lower radiating patches, two radiating nulls are introduced at the upper and lower edges of the passband, which enhances the filtering selectivity of the antenna. The finite element simulation software HFSS is used to simulate and optimize the filtenna model. The measurement results show that the impedance bandwidth of the filter antenna covers 24.23-29.41GHz. In the 5G frequency band N257 and N258, its S11 is less than -10dB, the average gain of the antenna is 6.12dBi, and the impedance bandwidth is 19.31%. Therefore, this filtenna could be a good candidate for millimeter wave 5G applications.

articleTitle: A 0.5W 33%-PAE Ka-band Power Amplifier in 0.15µm GaAs
abstract: This paper reports a 27–32 GHz 0.5-W monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) power amplifier (PA) fabricated in 0.15-µm GaAs pHEMT technology. With proposed matching method, the three stage PA achieves a flat small signal gain of 23-25.5 dB across a wide band. The measured power added efficiency (PAE) reaches a peak of 36%. The insertion loss of the 4-to-1 output power combiner is optimized to be less than 0.4 dB, obtaining the output power of 28.5 dBm at 1-dB compression point (P<inf>1dB</inf>), The chip occupies an area of 2×2.7 mm<sup>2</sup>.

articleTitle: An optimized input system for long-term prediction of cloud liquid water content
abstract: In this paper, an improved method for simulating cloud liquid water content in a space-earth laser communication scenario is presented. Cloud liquid water can block high frequency laser link, so it is necessary to consider the change of cloud liquid water in satellite-ground laser communication scenarios to determine the laser link blocking situation. The original Integrated Liquid Water Content (ILWC) synthesizer adopts the input method of using statistical data of cloud liquid water in a single point, which is not exactly accurate but applicable to the scene with fixed satellite receiving point. The improved linear interpolation method for cloud liquid water statistical data input improves the overall accuracy of the input data. The simulation results are more accurate when the ground satellite receiving point is mobile, and can be used for a better resource scheduling of a multi-ground station satellite communication network.

articleTitle: Meta Phase-Correcting-Surfaces and Feed Arrays for High-Gain Non-Resonant Partially Reflector Antennas (Invited paper)
abstract: Resonant Partially reflective surface (PRS) antennas have limited high-gain performance. This paper investigates and develops non-resonant PRS antennas loaded with a phase-correcting surface (PCS) and fed by a large inter-element spacing feed array. The PCS is used to provide the required compensation phases so that the waves above the PCS are in-phase and the main radiation beam can form. Hence, the high gain bandwidth can be obtained. Our simulation and analysis show that the gain performance improves with the increase of the element spacing of the feed array.

articleTitle: Study on the Symbol Error Probability of the NOMA-Based Hybrid Satellite- Terrestrial Relay Networks
abstract: In this paper, we consider the average symbol error probability (SEP) performance of a hybrid satellite-terrestrial relay network with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and decode-and-forward (DF) protocol. In particular, we derived the closed-form expression of the average SEP for both far-user and near-user in a satellite-to-terrestrial channel. Numerical results are presented to prove the correctness of the derived formulas and illustrate the effect of some pivotal factors on the average SEP of the considered system.

articleTitle: A Neural Network-Based Modeling Method for Terminal Charges in GaN HEMTs
abstract: In this paper, the detailed description of neural network (NN)-based modeling method for terminal charges in gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor (GaN HEMT) is presented. This method helps to overcome originally high modeling difficulty of terminal charges while their modeling accuracy can be guaranteed. A two-hidden layer ANN is constructed to model the source-end terminal charge (qis) and drain-end terminal charge (<tex>$q$</tex><inf>id</inf>) in the MIT Virtual Source (MVS) theory, respectively. The MVS theory is used to connect the ANN-based terminal charges and drain current. This method is benchmarked with accurate drain current performance.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Wide-angle Scanning Phased Array Antenna
abstract: In this work, a millimeter-wave wide-angle scanning phased array is proposed. The antenna consists of two rectangular metasurface cells and it is fed by a L probe, which can obtain a large impedance bandwidth and a wide beam in E-plane. Then, the 1×2 subarray is designed to construct a 8×2 wide-angle scanning phased array with the array spacing of 0.38 λ<inf>0</inf>. A grounded “II” structure is loaded between the antenna elements to improve the active S-parameters when the phased array is scanning. As results, the 10-dB impedance bandwidth of the proposed array can cover a wide band of 66-78GHz (16.7<sup>%</sup>). Moreover, it can scans up to ±65° in the whole operating band-width, while gain drop is less than 3 dB, and the maximum scan range reaches ±69°.

articleTitle: Intelligent classification system based on target detection algorithm and laser-SLAM algorithm
abstract: Currently, garbage classification and recycling have been a hot spot in society. The method of realizing garbage classification through manual manner is not only inefficient, high cost, but also in a harsh working environment. Therefore, through the research and application of technologies related to machine vision and autonomous driving, this paper designs an intelligent classification system based on YOLOv5 object detection algorithm and Gmapping laser-SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) algorithm to realize full-automation of garbage classification. The system vision module adopts YOLOv5 algorithm and trains the model on self-made garbage classification data set. U sing the trained model, the algorithm can extract the features of different types of garbage images to realize the purpose of garbage detection and classification. The movement control module adopts Gmapping algorithm based on LIDAR (Light Laser Detection and Ranging) to realize the synchronous positioning and map construction in the working environment, thereafter to complete the transportation of garbage. The experimental results show that the classification system designed in this paper can accurately transport the garbage to the destination with good intelligence.

articleTitle: Mode-reconfigurable OAM Transmitarray Based on A Novel Method
abstract: This paper presents mechanically mode-reconfigurable OAM (Orbit Angular Momentum) transmitarray based on a novel method. When different mechanic angles are rotated, transmitarray obtain different phase distributions. It's the first time to achieve mode-reconfigurable OAM beams based on the novel method without diodes during microwave region. To achieve the reconfigurable OAM beams, two kinds of transmissive elements are designed to form three transmitarrays. By rotating the third plate with 0°, 90°, 270° mechanically, the whole model can generate different mode 0, 1, -1 OAM beams. And simulation results indicate that the gain of 1, 0, -1 mode is 18.3dBi, 21.5dBi and 18.2dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: A Low-profile High Transparency Liquid Antenna Using Multi-layer Dielectric Structure in Microwave Region
abstract: We proposed a low-profile high transparency liquid antenna using two types of dielectric constant ionic liquid and multi-layer dielectric structure. The liquid antenna can consider as a dielectric resonant antenna(DRA) by using ionic liquid and resin container. By injecting various ionic liquid into different dielectric layer, which can excite the leaky radiating mode, the the high gain and wide-band performance have been achieved. The proposed antenna has frequency range from 13.19 GHz to 17.5 GHz(S11<-10dB) with a maximum gain is 17.9 dBi. Such antenna can be promising candidates for practical applications such as antenna designs and microwave circuits. More detailed work will be presented in the final paper.

articleTitle: Grey correlation analysis of strong electromagnetic environment and damage characteristics
abstract: Ships are often suffered from uncertain strong electromagnetic environment radiation during navigation, which always cause certain damage to their electrical equipment through coupling. In order to study the correlation characteristics between strong electromagnetic environment and damage characteristics, for the problems of information complexity and uncertainty in them. In this paper, the correlation analysis about complexity of their damage characteristics based on grey correlation is proposed. Combined with the physical characteristics of strong electromagnetic environment parameters, the correlation model of the corresponding coefficients is established, which shows that the model can find the main influencing factors from incomplete information. Thus, it can provide a effective solution for the strong electromagnetic protection process, improve the protection efficiency, verify the feasibility of this method through the measured data, and provide a better solution for the electromagnetic protection process in the future.

articleTitle: A Pulse Waveform Control Method for Multiple Harmonic Elimination of Multilevel RF-PWM
abstract: This paper presents a pulse waveform control method for multiple harmonic eliminations of multilevel RF-PWM. By considering the waveform synthesis of arbitrary multiple 3-level pulses, possible parameter groups of the pulses are obtained to eliminate multiple harmonics and make the fundamental component proportional to the input envelope. Taking the third and fifth harmonic elimination of multilevel RF-PWM as an example, two 3-level pulse waveform control methods are obtained. Each method can generate two different signal waveforms which have different influences on the performance of the output signal. The feasibility of the two methods and the effect of two waveforms on the performance are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Ultra-small All-Optical Logic Gate Design based on Inverse Design for Wire-less Communication
abstract: This article introduces the inverse design into the all-optical logic gates. Using direct-binary search (DBS) and the adjoint method, the ultra-small XOR logic gate is designed, and the size is only 1.2um*2.5um, which is the smallest record known so far. The device with parallel logic function in C-band and O-band is realized for the first time. All designs conform to standard processes, laying the foundation for the development of optical computing and optical neural networks.

articleTitle: A 2-D Envelope Combination Selective Affine Function-Based Behavioral Model for Concurrent Dual-Band Power Amplifiers
abstract: A novel 2-D envelope combination selective affine function-based (2D-ECSA) behavioral model is proposed for linearization of the concurrent dual-band power amplifiers (PAs). The core of the model is to use two independent envelope combination selective affine (ECSA) functions to replace the high-order terms composed of the input envelopes of the existing 2-D simplified memory polynomial (2D-SMP) model, respectively. The proposed 2D-ECSA model can be regarded as the superposition of two linear structures, which can further reduce the computational complexity and the actual hardware resource occupation of the 2D-SMP model. Experimental results fully demonstrate that compared with the original model, the proposed model can provide similar normalized mean square error (NMSE) and digital predistortion (DPD) performance when a PAis driven by two concurrent 20-MHz signals.

articleTitle: A Broadband Fully Integrated GaAs Power Amplifier Using FDCS Bandpass Filtering Matching Network
abstract: In this paper, a wideband bandpass filtering matching network (MN), with frequency-dependent complex source (FDCS) and standard 50 Ω load, is analyzed and designed. The adoption of mutual inductance introduces a transmission zero for improving frequency selectivity, and decoupling equivalently reduces chip size. By co-designing the output matching network (OMN) with FDCS MN, a fully integrated bandpass filtering power amplifier (BPF-PA) is presented and built on the GaAs HBT process. The proposed PA exhibits good broadband filtering performance, smooth in-band gain, and high PAE.

articleTitle: A Time-Frequency-Domain Method of TDOA Estimation for Passive Radar Localization
abstract: A time-frequency-domain method of TDOA estimation is proposed in this paper. Time-domain correlation and frequency-domain estimation are used together to improve the accuracy of estimation. In this method, a new strategy consists of time shifting, slicing and least squares approximation is applied to eliminate the limitation of radar sampling frequency. A Monte Carlo simulation is conducted to evaluate the performance of this method. Additionally, the typical radar signal of AN/SPY-1 is chosen to be testing signal. The result indicates that the time-frequency-domain method could obtain 71 % performance improvements. In addition, it proves to be an effective solution to TDOA estimation for passive radar localization.

articleTitle: P/L-Band 60W Broadband GaN Power Amplifier Compact Module
abstract: In order to meet the demand of broadband miniaturized solid-state power amplifiers for radar systems, a high efficiency power amplifier was designed and implemented using a 0.5um GaN HEMT process. The power amplifier is realized by using passive elements on substrates with different permittivity for reducing the size and a compact broadband matching topology for broadband. The experimental results at pulse excitation show that the power amplifier output power is larger than 60W, the gain is over 31dB, and the power added efficiency (PAE) is more than 55% in the 700-1250MHz frequency band, which has a record relative bandwidth over 56% in P/L band over 60W output power.

articleTitle: Optical transparent microwave absorber for high-quality imaging
abstract: The optical transparency of the microwave absorber is always emphasized, the effect of uneven transmittance which affects the imaging was ignored, thereby hindering further window application. Under the limitation of using uniform film, an absorber using transparent conductive film is designed for good-visual perception inspired by the Jaumann screen. Through adjusting impedance matching of the structure, the proposed absorber achieves 90% absorption in the range of 9.4 to 26 GHz (fractional bandwidth 93.7%). Meanwhile, the proposed structure measures 76.6% transmittance and 0.37% haze, denoting the application potential. It is believed that the proposed design strategy promotes the practicality process of transparent absorbers.

articleTitle: Antennas Optimal Design Using Opposition-Based Learning and Altruistic Aquila Optimizer Algorithm
abstract: In order to improve the working performance of the monopole dual-band antenna, this paper proposes a hybrid Aquila optimization (HAO) based on opposition-based learning strategy and altruism to optimize the parameters of the monopole antenna. HAO enhances the diversity of the algorithm population through opposition-based learning strategy, improves the algorithm convergence speed, and integrates altruism to improve the algorithm's ability to jump out of the local optimum. The HAO is compared with the unimodal benchmark and Multimodal benchmark test functions, and the test results show that the HAO has better performance. Finally, EAO successfully optimized a dual-band monopole antenna that can work in 2.4/5.2GHz WLAN systems.

articleTitle: The Design of a 57-65GHz SPDT Switch with LC Resonant Techniques in 40 nm CMOS Process
abstract: This paper presents a single-pole double-throw (SPDT), transmit/receive (T/R) switch operating from 57 to 65GHz in 40 nm CMOS process. The SPDT is based on series-shunt transistors circuit with input and output matching networks. By using LC resonant techniques, the isolation of the switch in mil-limeter wave band can be improved by selecting appropriate res-onant inductors. The SPDT switch results in simulated insertion loss of 2.7dB at 60GHz and isolation is better than 28dB from 57 to 65GHz with return loss less than -13dB. With a control voltage of 1.2 V, the IP1dB of the switch is 12.7dBm at 60GHz. The core area size of switch is <tex>$0.178\times 0.117$</tex> mm2.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-Way In-Phase Feeding Networks with Arbitrary Power Distribution Based on SIW Cavity
abstract: In this paper, a new method to design multi-way in-phase feeding networks with arbitrary power distribution is proposed based on a circular substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity. The electric-field distribution of the TE<inf>101</inf> mode in a circular SIW cavity is inspected to guide the design. Analysis results show that arbitrary power splitting ratio can be achieved by arranging output feeding points at proper positions. In order to verify the design concept, an eight-way SIW feeding network with different power distribution is designed. Finally, measured results, agreeing well with simulated ones, is provided and show that the proposed network operates at 11.52 GHz with a 10 dB bandwidth of 13.2%. The networks in this paper can serve as a good candidate for low-sidelobe antenna arrays application.

articleTitle: RFI Localization Using Joint Sparsity Property in Interferometric Radiometer
abstract: In this paper, a new model using the joint sparsity property (JSP) is proposed to locate radio frequency interference (RFI) sources by the multi-snapshot data from the satellite named Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS). The JSP model can be solved by exploiting the row-sparsity property of multi-snapshot data. The numerical simulation result reveals that the proposed JSP model performs better on location accuracy than the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) method.

articleTitle: Mitigation of UWB Radar Self-Motion for mm-Scale Vibration Detection
abstract: To reliably detect a target's mm-scale vibration with a handheld ultra-wideband (UWB) radar system, it is essential to mitigate radar self-motion (RSM) caused by unavoidable hand shaking. In this paper, to further mitigate the effect of stationary objects surrounding the target in real deployment environment, a more practical RSM signal model is proposed. Affected by adjacent objects and RSM, traditional variance-based target positioning method becomes unreliable and the quality of target signal degrades severely as the target's position is often estimated inaccurately. To tackle this problem, an extended bin selection strategy is adopted by considering multiple range bins around the target and independent component analysis (ICA) is leveraged to separate target motion and RSM. Experiments are conducted to verify the proposed technique, and a mm-scale mechanical vibration is reliably detected from 0.5-2m away with the handheld UWB radar system, achieving a median frequency estimation error rate lower than 3.7% under different adjacent environments.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-Loaded Pattern Reconfigurable Dielectric Resonator Antenna for 5G Multi-Beam Base Station Applications
abstract: This work proposes a compact mushroom-loaded pattern steerable antenna using the Huygens theory for 5G-NR antenna applications. The compact vertically polarized (VP) dielectric resonator (DR) antenna with a low profile of 0.09 λ<inf>0</inf> is achieved by integrating the periodic metamaterial and the DR radiator. Using the Huygens radiation principle, a novel miniaturized pattern steerable DR antenna/radiator with eight switchable end-fire patterns is achieved by only adopting four switch diodes. The proposed beam steerable radiator as the array element is used in a 4 × 4 inexpensive large-angle beam-steering array. Owing to the tilted beam, the beam steering region of the presented 2D phased array can extend from [−35°, 35°] to [−75°, 75°]. The half-power beam-width (HPBW) can cover [−102°, 102°] in each plane. With the merits of a compact, broadband, inexpensive, and large-angle scanning/coverage capacity, this design is a promising candidate for smart antenna systems and 5G-NR multi-beam applications.

articleTitle: Design of FSS Using Equivalent Circuit and MOPSO algorithm
abstract: In this paper, a design method of frequency selective surface (FSS) using an equivalent circuit (EC) and multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) algorithm is proposed in this paper. The EC with the desired frequency response is established first. Then the initial structure is determined based on the EC and building blocks. Finally, the structure parameters are optimized using the MOPSO algorithm. It was applied to the triple pass-band FSS, and the analysis of the results shows that such the global scan method can obtain the target FSS more swiftly and accurately.

articleTitle: Retro-reflective Beamforming to Multiple Targets Based on Time-reversal for Microwave Power Transmission
abstract: This paper presents an experimental retro-reflective beamforming system based on time-reversal for wireless power transmission to multiple target devices. In this experiment, the wireless power transmitter with a four-element antenna array receives pilot signals from three targets, each at a unique frequency. The pilot signals containing multiple frequencies are down-converted to baseband, and then, an FPGA is used to re-verse the baseband signal in time to achieve phase conjugation of the signals at all frequencies. With a digital beamforming circuit architecture, the reversed signals are up-converted, and after amplification, fed to the antenna array. As a result, multiple ret-ro-reflective beams are formed, each at a unique frequency and toward a different target. The results show that the experimental system is able to simultaneously focus power onto three targets dynamically, which validates the effectiveness of the multi-target retro-reflective beamforming schemes.

articleTitle: Circular Patch MIMO Antenna with Novel Decoupling Structure
abstract: A two-port circular patch antenna with a novel de-coupling structure for multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) application is proposed. The slim metal plates and the metallic screws are utilized to construct a pair of series resonators, which provide a high port isolation for the antenna. Owing to this proposed decoupling structure, only one radiating patch is needed and a compact dimension of <tex>$\pi\times(0.25\lambda_{0})^{2}\times 0.06)\lambda_{0}$</tex> is achieved. The measured -10 dB impedance bandwidth is 3.21-3.52 GHz (9.2<sup>%</sup>). A measured port isolation better than 18.6 dB is realized in the operating band and the peak value achieves 44.1 dB. Measured efficiency is higher than 83 % and peak gain is about 6.5 dBi. Finally, a three-port antenna based on the same principle is proposed. Overall, the proposed two antennas with a compact structure, high port isolation and good radiation performance are suitable for MIMO application.

articleTitle: A Dual-polarized Tightly Coupled Antenna Array with Small Scale
abstract: A dual-polarized tightly coupled antenna element and an antenna array are presented with an impedance bandwidth ratio of 2.5:1 covering 0.8-2GHz. The power is fed through an exponentially graded balun, and the VSWR of the antenna element is less than 2. Based on the antenna model, an antenna array with small scale is fabricated with VSWR less than 2.2.

articleTitle: Efficient Microwave Rectifier With Minimized Size
abstract: In this paper, an efficient and minimized rectifier using lumped inductors and capacitors is introduced. To simplify the design, an inductor is used to cancel the imaginary part of the Schottky diode for the input matching circuit design. Then, a LC lowpass filter is designed to suppress the RF signal at the DC output port. To demonstrate, a 2.45 GHz rectifier is designed and fabricated. Thanks to the lumped components, The fabricated rectifier only occupies an area of 15 mm X 10 mm. The fabricated rectifier exhibits a peak power conversion efficiency of 76.7% when the input power is 11 dBm. Our design proves that the lumped components can be used in the high efficiency rectifier design at the frequencies below 3 GHz which will benefit minimized rectifier design.

articleTitle: 2 × 2 Dual-Polarized Phased Array Testbench for 5G NR Communication and Video Transmission
abstract: This paper presents a <tex>$2 \times 2$</tex> dual-polarized phased array testbench for fifth-generation (5G) communication system and video transmission. The transceiver chip is integrated with <tex>$2 \times2$</tex> dual-polarized antenna array on the printed circuit board (PCB). The antenna array has rotated feed design with more than 22 dB cross-polarization rejection at broadside. The antenna element can achieve a -10 dB impendence bandwidth of 3.25 GHz (24.25-27.5 GHz) and the array presents a measured effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) at P1dB of 29 dBm and scans <tex>$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex> in azimuth at 26 GHz. For validating its performance for 5G applications, dual-polarized communication link of 5G new radio (NR) signal of 400 MHz using two phased arrays is demonstrated. The error vector magnitude (EVM) degraded less than 0.1 % for dual-polarization operation compared to the single-polarization one. Also, the 1080p video transmission is validated by employing two phased arrays.

articleTitle: Photoacoustic Image Guidance for Acupuncture
abstract: There is currently a lack of a visualized tool to study the acupuncture therapy. In this study, we developed a noninvasive and fast photoacoustic tomography technique to realize image guidance for acupuncture. We implemented a rapid data collection scheme through a handheld array-transducer and a multi-channel data acquisition subsystem to realize a real-time photoacoustic imaging system with high sensitivity and spatial resolution. Neiguan point (PC 6) is selected as the stimulating points in human being. Real-time photoacoustic images of the position of needle relative to the surrounding tissue and the distribution of vascular system of in the cross section of arm at Neiguan point before and during acupuncture are obtained at 760 nm. Ultrasound imaging results were used as cross validation. Our results suggest that PAT could provide image guidance for acupuncture, and may have great potential for standard location of acupoints.

articleTitle: W-Band $8\times 8$ Slot Array Antenna Using Hybrid Processing Technology of Silicon Micromachining and Metal Machining
abstract: In this paper, a multilayer W-band <tex>$8\times 8$</tex> slot array antenna processed using hybrid technology of silicon micromachining and metal machining is presented. The proposed antenna is composed of four silicon layers for radiating part and two metal layers for feeding network. Adjacent gold-plated silicon substrates and the metal cover plate are connected by gold-gold bonding. Using bulk silicon processing, high fabrication accuracy is realized for the 94-GHz large-scale array antenna. Metal-machining gap waveguide with artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) structure is elaborated for the corporate feeding network. Each <tex>$2\times 2$</tex>-elements slots subarray is excited by the TM240-mode cavity element below. Besides, a structural transition from standard waveguide WR-10 to gap waveguide is employed. Simulated results indicate that the proposed antenna can achieve 6.4 % <tex>$(\vert \mathrm{S}11\vert < -10\text{dB})$</tex> operating bandwidth covering from 91.2 to 97.27 GHz, with the gain greater than 26.1 dBi. The proposed antenna has the merits of high gain, heterogeneous integration and low cost, promising usage in various millimeter-wave wireless systems.

articleTitle: A Horizontal Gradual Ultra-Low-Reflection Stripline to Grounded Coplanar Waveguide Transition
abstract: In this letter, a horizontal gradual low-reflection stripline (SL) to ground coplanar waveguide (GCPW) transition is proposed, which consists of a gradient SL transition with a non-linear gradient slot and a GCPW transition with two extra ground plates. To measure performance of the proposed SL-to-GCPW transition, a back-to-back GCPW-SL-GCPW structure is designed and fabricated under low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) process. Simulation and measurement results agree well. The results show the bandwidth of the proposed transition up to 110GHz. From DC to 67 GHz, the return loss and insertion loss are larger than 15 dB and less than 0.8 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: An Integrated Broadband MMW Antenna Using Multilayer PCB
abstract: In this paper, a novel integrated broadband millimeter wave (MMW) antenna is presented by using multilayer PCB with buried multimode resonator. A stepped back cavity is introduced under the slotted microstrip patch to improve the radiation and impedance matching bandwidth. This scheme is used to design a MMW antenna to cover the 5G communication frequency band from 24.5 GHz to 29.5 GHz. The integrated antenna is designed and fabricated using six layers of printed circuit board. Maximum gain of 8 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: A Double-Sided Printed Crossed Dipole Antenna with Enhanced Impedance and FBR Performance for Circularly Polarized Applications
abstract: A broadband dipole antenna for circularly polarized (CP) applications is presented in this paper. The antenna consists of a crossed dipole, four parasitic patches, four metallic sidewalls and a metallic reflector. The crossed dipole radiator is fed by a 90° phase delay ring, generating CP radiation. Besides, the newly created CP mode is produced herein by using the parasitic patches. Hence, the CP bandwidth combining with the original CP mode is greatly expanded. Finally, the sidewall is introduced to enhance front-back ratio (FBR) performance. The proposed antenna is simulated, and the results indicate impendence band-width is 54.5% (1.28-2.24 GHz), and 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 35.3% (1.4-2.0 GHz). Furthermore, the proposed antenna achieves good FBR radiation performance over the en-tire frequency band, about 24 dB.

articleTitle: An Efficient 2 × 64-Element Dual-Linearly-Polarized Dual-Beam Phased Array for 5G mmWave Communications
abstract: In this paper, an efficient 2 × 64-element dual-linearly-polarized (dual-LP) dual-beam phased array is proposed for 5G millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication. Since the array consists of two separate 8 × 8 single-linearly-polarized subarrays in the vertical and horizontal polarization, respectively, the couple between the different polarizations is reduced. Each antenna element is a probe-fed 2-element patch antenna array, which improves the total radiated power (TRP) and power efficiency by sacrificing the scanning angle in the vertical plane. The measured horizontal-polarization effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) at P1dB is 60.14 dBm, while the vertical-polarization EIRP at P1dB is 57.84dBm. Measured results under simultaneous dual-stream operation show that the array could work as a 5G polarization-based multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) system when scanning from −20° to 25° in the horizontal plane.

articleTitle: Digital Predistortion of RF Power Amplifiers Considering the Group Delay Distortion
abstract: In this paper, a novel adaptive time alignment method for digital predistortion (DPD) is proposed to deal with the linearization of power amplifiers (PAs) when severer group delay distortion (GDD) exists in the feedback path. Group delay mismatch significantly influences the precision during the extraction of the DPD model's coefficients. Based on the mathematical analysis of group delay, the proposed method can weaken the effects of GDD. Experiments' results confirm that the DPD model with the proposed method has better performance than the DPD model only with the traditional time alignment method.

articleTitle: A Near-field Imaging Algorithm for Synthetic Aperture Interferometric Radiometers
abstract: Near-field imaging of synthetic aperture interfero-metric radiometers (SAIR) is discussed. If the scene plane is parallel to the array plane, the near-field visibility function can be represented as the convolution results of brightness temperature (BT) distribution and a kernel function. Therefore, the near-field imaging process of SAIR is a deconvolution operation. This paper presents a frequency-domain-based (FDB) algorithm for near-field SAIR. First, weighting the visibility function by the redundancy factor. Second, the algorithm exploits the deconvolution operation with frequency domain to reconstruct the 4-D image domain data. Finally, the BT image is reconstructed via a dimension-reducing operation. The imaging experiment shows that the presented method can reconstruct the passive millimeter-wave (PMMW) image.

articleTitle: Independent phase and amplitude controlled transmitarray antenna with high gain and low sidelobes
abstract: A novel transmitarray antenna (TA) consisted of the element which is proposed to achieve the capability to control the transmission phase and magnitude independently by simply changing two geometric parameters of it. The structure works as the element of the TA can cover 360°phase range and the desired magnitude distribution. The advantages of this design are more flexibility to adjust the phase and magnitude to enable the TA to get high gain and low SLLs directly and efficiently. The simulated results verify the design concept.

articleTitle: Recent Developments in Space Mapping Methods for EM Optimization
abstract: Space mapping (SM) is an acknowledged approach for speeding up electromagnetic (EM) optimization. To further speed up the optimization process, it is necessary to take more efficient and general SM methods. This article gives a review of the recent developments in SM optimization exploiting parallel SM approach as well as coarse- and fine-mesh SM comprising mesh morphing. Two microwave applications are used to illustrate these approaches.

articleTitle: Interference graph based knapsack clustering algorithm in ultra-dense networks
abstract: To solve the problem of high inter-cell interference in ultra-dense networks, this paper proposes an interfer-ence graph based knapsack clustering algorithm. Firstly, the weighted undirected interference graph is drawn by measuring the reference signal receiving power (RSRP) of adjacent base stations (BSs) through user equipment (UE). On this basis, the clustering result matches the distribution of user service through dynamic programming, in which avoiding intra-cluster interference and minimizing inter-cluster interference serve as a criterion. The simulation results show that compared with traditional clustering algorithm, the proposed algorithm effectively improves the satisfaction rate of user service as well as system throughput.

articleTitle: Design of Ridged Structural Composite Transmission Line
abstract: In this paper, a structural composite transmission line composed of the ridged substrate integrated waveguide (RSIW) and the embedded ground coplanar waveguide (GCPW) is proposed for parallel transmission of multi-mode signals. The structure makes full use of the waveguide space to efficiently excite the TE20 mode of the RSIW and the quasi- TEM mode of the GCPW without increasing the number of substrate layers. Simulation results show that the insertion loss <tex>$\vert S_{21}\vert$</tex> of the RSIW is less than 1.3dB, and <tex>$\vert S_{43}\vert$</tex> of the GCPW is less than O.5dB within their respective working bandwidth. The isolation <tex>$\vert S_{31}\vert$</tex> between the two waveguides is greater than 55dB. The proposed structural composite transmission line would be attractive for future multi-frequency and multi-function system.

articleTitle: Detection of psoriatic arthritis in the finger joints by Thermoacoustic Tomography
abstract: Psoriatic arthritis is also known as arthropathic psoriasis, and can ultimately lead to j oint destruction and functional disabilities. Current clinical imaging techniques to assess psoriatic arthritis have their own advantages and disadvantages. The demand for sensitive and efficient tools for the diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis is on the rise. Here, as a novel imaging modality, thermoacoustic tomography was used to evaluate psoriatic arthritis. The preliminary result indicated that TAT images of the psoriatic arthritis joint showed differences in tissue structures and image contrast compared to the healthy ones. Therefore, the pilot study provides a foundation for TAT futher clinical validation to the diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis.

articleTitle: A High Linearity Class AB Power Amplifier for Sub-1 GHz Applications
abstract: In this paper, a 400MHz class-AB power amplifier (PA) with high linearity and output power is presented. This two-stage PA consists of on-chip power transistors and off-chip tunable LC load networks for reducing the chip cost due to the low operating frequency. Based on the linearity-oriented optimization of matching networks, the iterative circuit/EM co-simulation of the integrated circuit, package, and PCB levels is accomplished to minimize the discrepancy between the simulation and measurement results. The design is implemented in 130 nm CMOS technology with a core area of 0.13 mm<sup>2</sup>. Measurement results show that the PA delivers an output 1-dB compression of 18.1 dBm under 2.5 V voltage supply. Moreover, it achieves a saturated power of 24.2 dBm with a maximum gain of 27.8 dB and power-added efficiency (PAE) of 43.8%.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile All-Dielectric Circularly Polarized Ring Antenna Made of 3-D Printed Zirconia Ceramic
abstract: This paper proposes a low-profile circularly polarized ring antenna entirely made of zirconia ceramic. It possesses an all-in-one structure where a ceramic plate with probe feed is connected to the two terminals of a ceramic three-quarter ring. The main part of ring is parallel to the plate with a small gap. The radiation of high-permittivity dielectric waveguide under cut-off region of TM<inf>01</inf> mode is here utilized in the proposed antenna. By virtue of 3-D printing technology, the proposed antenna with curly structure can be easily formed. Besides, different from other dielectric antennas with metal ground plane, the proposed antenna is all-dielectric so as to attain a lower radar cross section (RCS). The proposed antenna can also achieve wide impedance and axial ratio bandwidths. Finally, an all-dielectric ring antenna prototype with an axial ratio bandwidth from 5.5 to 6.5 GHz is designed. Its impedance, radiation and scattering characteristics are here investigated.

articleTitle: Full-Angle Digital Predistortion Technique for 5G Millimeter-Wave Integrated Phased Array
abstract: In this paper, a full-angle digital predistortion (DPD) technique is proposed to linearize fifth-generation (5G) millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) integrated phased array transmitters with low complexity. The far-field main beam is captured as the feedback signal for the DPD system which is cascaded by the ΔDPD array and the Ref-DPD block. The former is implemented to compensate the differences between different angles and the latter is used to linearize the whole system. Applied in a 64-channel integrated phased array working at 28 GHz, the proposed method can enhance the EIRP of transmitter by more than 6 dB under the constraints of EVM and ACPR. The number of coefficients can be reduced by 64% without obvious performance degradation.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Wideband Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna with AMC
abstract: This paper proposes a magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna with low profile and wideband characteristics based on artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) structures. The zero-phase reflection surface is composed of two AMC structures, which can reduce the profile of proposed antenna to <tex>$0.124\lambda_{0}\ (\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the free-space wavelength of center frequency). The profile height is reduced by 32.5% when compared to the typical ME dipole antenna in the same dielectric substrate. Furthermore, the proposed AMC structure has the similar characteristic to the electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure, which can suppress the propagation of surface wave and lessen the coupling impact between the antenna in the array. By simulation, the impedance bandwidth of this antenna is 39.1 % (from 8.25 to 12.16GHz) for <tex>$\mathrm{S}_{11} < -10\text{dB}$</tex>. Additionally, the ME dipole antenna has a stable gain about 6.3dBi and the beam-width of <tex>$\pm 46^{\circ}$</tex> in the band. In the operating frequency, the <tex>$1\times 8$</tex> one-dimensional array composed of ME dipole antennas can scan <tex>$\pm 53^{\circ}$</tex>, which is suitable for use in a X-band phased array.

articleTitle: Complex-amplitude metalens with extended depth of focus and enhanced focal uniformity
abstract: Deep depth of focus (DoF) metalenses have wide application prospects in the fields of security inspection, biological observation, and 3D imaging. However, prevailing design approaches have inherent defects such as numerical aperture (NA) constraints and poor focal uniformity. To conquer these limitations, a complex-amplitude (CA) deep DoF metalens is demonstrated in the microwave region, enabled by the marriage of a novel 3D CA retrieval method and the C-shaped meta-atoms. An extended DoF of 6.9λ can be simulated, corresponding to the NA range from 0.8725 to 0.4582. Meanwhile, the lateral focal spot is uniformly distributed longitudinally, with the variance value of 21.03 in the focal spot diameter. The proposed retrieval method can provide an optimized design strategy for the deep DoF metalens, ensuring the DoF accuracy and the focal uniformity. The numerical comparison results prove the validity and superiority of this method.

articleTitle: An Active Coding-Feeding Metasurface with Polarization Conversion and Radiation Manipulation
abstract: This letter proposes an active coding-feeding metasurface based on PIN diodes which achieves incidence polarization conversion and radiation manipulation simultaneously. The topological structure of metasurface is designed and its different performances are invested by numerical simulation. The simulation demonstrates that the metasurface can realize polarization conversation at 5.93-6.41 GHz and reflection at 5.93-6.55GHz like a metal plate by switching PIN diodes state and radiate efficiently at 7.27- 7.56GHz and 8.16-8.51GHz. The multifunctional active metasurface will have potential application in radio communication systems.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Beamforming System Based on Active Antenna Array with Stacked Patch Filtenna
abstract: Towards the demand of affordable beamforming systems with satisfactory performance and size specification, an 8 x 8 hybrid beamforming (HBF) system based on active antenna array (AAA) is presented in this paper. Different from the existing AAAs with dipole antennas connected with active circuits by connectors, in the proposed design, low-profile patch filtennas are employed and connectors are replaced with PCB metal holes, further decreasing the overall size and insertion loss significantly. Besides, the proposed filtenna exhibits a quasi-elliptic filtering response without extra filtering circuits. Measured results show that the active circuits perform a low gain variation and a low noise figure both below 1.5dB, and the filtenna performs a wide bandwidth from 3.2GHz to 3.7GHz and two radiation nulls at 2.4GHz and 4.9GHz. The HBF system exhibits a compact configuration and a good beam steering capability in the range from - 40deg to 40deg.

articleTitle: Robustness Enhancement Technique and Fine-Tuning Technique of IIP3 for Wideband LNTA
abstract: Wideband low noise transconductance amplifier(LNTA) is an essential part of current-mode SAW-less receivers, and its linearity design is the most challenging. Many low noise amplifier(LNA) linearization techniques(LT) are also applicable to LNTA, such as the famous derivative superposition(DS) and post-distortion(PD). But these techniques are not robust and are prone to failure. This paper is based on a noise canceling(NC) LNTA prototype and improves its performance in several aspects with some unique analysis. The robustness of the IIP3 of the original LNTA is enhanced by using a self-biasing network. By changing the connection of the DS MOSFETs, the sensitivity of the IIP3 to the load resistance is reduced. Finally, by adopting PD as a fine-tuning technique in the right place, the IIP3 of the LNTA is improved to more than 20dBm.

articleTitle: A Compact Simultaneous Transmit and Receive Antenna with Circular Mode Phasing for Smartphones
abstract: This article discusses the design progression of the simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) antenna applied to in-band full-duplex (IBFD) applications. Specifically, this antenna system is composed of four slots and a patch, and integrated into a mobile. The slot modes together with patch mode is analyzed, and the placement of the antennas is designed. The theoretical circular mode phasing is given along with simulation results. The proposed antenna can provide up to 70 dB of isolation over the desired frequencies. This system is with low profile, compact, high isolated performances, indicating the potential applications of high-rate, high-capacity, low-time delay terminal wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Aperture Coupled Patch Antenna Array Based on High Integration PCB Design
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile aperture coupled patch antenna array for anti-UAV mobile system and satellite communication on-the-move system. This antenna array utilizes <tex>$4\times 2$</tex> patch antenna elements with high integration PCB board design. The H-shaped slot is etched on the ground plane to couple signal power to realize wide bandwidth radiation. The proposed array is excited by the strip line network below the H-shaped slot to realize beam pattern. The prototype of this array is fabricated and measured to verify the design. The -10 dB impedance band-width of proposed antenna array achieves bandwidth of 24.5% in X-band. The proposed array has a peak gain of 15.1 dBi, while the cross polarization is under -24 dB.

articleTitle: A Linearity-enhanced 28-GHz Class-F−1 SiGe Power Amplifier
abstract: This paper presents a Class-F<sup>−1</sup> power amplifier (PA) targeting 28-GHz 5G communication. A common emitter (CE) topology with a degeneration inductor for linearity enhancement is analyzed. The optimum harmonic terminations for Class-F<sup>−1</sup> operation are provided by a transformer-based harmonic tuned network. Fabricated in <tex>$0.13-\mu \text{mSiGe}$</tex> process, the PA achieves a measured output 1-dB compression point <tex>$(\text{OP}_{1\text{dB}})$</tex> of 16.5 dBm and a maximum power-added efficiency (PAE) of 37.2% at 28 GHz with a 1.6-V supply. The high linearity of the PA is demonstrated by a 64-QAM signal measurement with 2.4 Gb/s data rate at 28 GHz. The proposed PA exhibits a 12.5-dBm average output power (P<inf>avg</inf>) and 17.8% PAE with a corresponding EVM of -26 dB. The proposed PA fulfills the high linearity and high efficiency requirement of 5G applications.

articleTitle: Characterization Parameter of Material Information in Passive Millimeter-wave Sensing
abstract: Passive millimeter-wave (MMW) sensing has been used for several close-range applications such as security checks, military detection, terrain modeling, and so on. By measuring the electromagnetic energy radiated by different materials, it is pos-sible to distinguish them. However, the brightness temperature (TB) can not be directly used for material classification, and those TB-derived material discriminators are not stable charac-terization parameters. In this article, we analyze the multi-polarization brightness temperature model and propose the equivalent permittivity (EP) to characterize the material infor-mation. This parameter, to some extent, is not affected by inci-dent angle and can be derived by multi-polarization measure-ment. The significant advantage of EP is that it reduces the di-mension of parameters in the model. Therefore, it is conducive to extracting object information based on the MMW radiation model. As an application example, we used EP in this article for object classification. Based on EP, we successfully classified four objects with an accuracy of about 99%. Future applications of our method include liquid analysis and scene monitoring.

articleTitle: A 52.5GHz-66GHz High Conversion Gain Frequency Tripler using $.13\mu \text{m SiGe}$ HBT process
abstract: A 52.5GHz-66GHz frequency tripler using <tex>$0.13\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> SiGe HBT process is presented, which adopts a single balanced structure, with a high conversion gain up to 14.3dB. A maximum saturated output power <tex>$(\mathrm{P}_{\text{sat}})$</tex> up to 12.3dBm@57GHz is measured, with a 3-dB bandwidth of 13.5GHz (22.7<sup>%</sup> relative bandwidth). A folded marchand balun is applied to transform single-end signals into differential ones, with an amplitude difference less than 0.5dB and a phase difference within <tex>$180\pm 6$</tex> degrees. A gain enhancing technique is also adopted. The chip size is <tex>$620\mu\mathrm{m}\times 200\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> without pads and <tex>$880\mu\mathrm{m}\times520\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> altogether.

articleTitle: Joint Antenna Decoupling and Beamspace Transform for Digital Antenna Array
abstract: In 5G mobile communication systems, mutual coupling compensation is necessary for antenna arrays to obtain high-quality pattern with very low sidelobes and deep deterministic nullings. Meanwhile, beamspace transform is promising to reduce complexity in array processing. Traditionally, these two techniques are implemented separately. In this paper, a technique is presented for both mutual coupling compensation and beamspace transform in a digital antenna array. Mathematically, the scheme can be readily implemented in a digital antenna array with low complexity. Simulation results have confirmed the correctness and effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A 28-GHz Current-Mode Outphasing Power Amplifier with Peak PAE of 51 % and OP1dB of 22.89dBm for 5G Applications
abstract: This paper presents a 28-GHz current-mode power combining outphasing power amplifer (P A). Each P A cell utilizes source degeneration to achieve high linearity while maintaining high gain and high output power. A current-mode power combiner is optimized for Chireix compensation and minimum insertion loss. Designed in TSMC 40nm LP CMOS process, the proposed outphasing P A achieves a peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 51 %, a 6-dB power back-off (PBO) PAE of 27.82%, and an output power 1-dB compression point (OP1dB) of 22.89dBm in post-layout simulation results.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis and Design of RF Power Harvesters for 50-IoT Applications
abstract: In this paper, a theoretical model was proposed for analyzing RF rectifiers. It can calculate the diode power conversion efficiency (PCE), input impedance, rectifier matching efficiency, and total output dc power (or total PCE). This model can achieve a high accuracy (< 5% error) over a wide frequency and power range. For demonstration, a dual-band RF rectifier is proposed to cover two 5G frequency bands in China. Besides, a miniaturized wideband dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) was developed to provide omnidirectional radiation patterns. The DRA and rectifier can be integrated forming a RF power harvester for powering wireless sensor network nodes in the 5G enabled IoT applications.

articleTitle: Stealth Target Detection Based on Vortex Microwave Photons with a Rotational Antenna
abstract: It has been confirmed that the echo powers of the specific target are different for different OAM modes, which is helpful for stealth target detection. Besides, when the absorbing materials are illuminated by vortex microwave photons, the higher receiving power can be achieved. Therefore, this paper investigates a stealth target detection system based on vortex microwave photons with a rotational antenna. In the proposed detection system, the high order vortex beams can be synthesized with a rotational antenna. In addition, vortex microwave photons can be generated by interacting with vortex electrons. Afterwards, the corresponding mathematical models are established to explain the echo power improvement for the stealth target. Furthermore, simulations are implemented to evaluate the receiving power. It is demonstrated that the proposed detection system based on vortex microwave photons with a rotational antenna can result in an obvious receiving power gain compared with the traditional detection system with plane waves.

articleTitle: Vortex Beam Generation based on Digital Coding Transmissive Metasurface
abstract: Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) is a phenomenon of vortex wavefront for electromagnetic wave. Due to the characteristics of infinite orthogonal modes, it has profound potential in promoting communication capability. Here, a digital coding transmissive metasurface based on Pancharatnam-Berry phase principle has been presented to realize OAM with <tex>$l=+5$</tex> mode and purity of 93% in 9.3GHz. The continuous phase shifting is achieved by rotating the metasurface element. Afterwards, the simulated results illustrate the well performance of proposed metasurface, which is coincide with the theoretical results. The proposed digital coding transmissive metasurface has potential application in wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Spectrum Aliasing-Free All Digital RF -PWM Transmitter Using Sine Wave Reference
abstract: To reduce the complex implementation of existing spectrum aliasing-free all-digital radio frequency digital pulse width modulation (RF-PWM) in engineering, a novel RF-PWM all-digital transmitter (ADTx) architecture using sine wave as the reference signal is presented. Four pairs of mutually orthogonal sine wave groups are used as the reference signals of the I and Q quadrature differential PWM units respectively, delta-sigma modulator and digital predistortion are used to suppress modulation noise and spectral aliasing. As a result, alias-free pulse coding can be realized, and the even harmonic components are also suppressed. The feasibility of this novel RF-PWM ADTx is demonstrated, and the system performance is verified by Q PSK and 16QAM signals. Simulation and measurement results show that when compared with the existing RF-PWM ADTx which uses triangular wave as the reference signal, the in-band signal quality and modulation performance of the proposed scheme is similar, but the complexity is much lower.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Spherical 3D Imaging Ultrasound Array Probe
abstract: We designed a hemispherical ultrasound array transducer to obtain high-resolution 3D images for photoacoustic tomography. It can be used to detect all kinds of signals. In order to obtain high-resolution three-dimensional images, we place as many piezoelectric transducers as possible in the hemisphere. And the receiving frequency band of the transducer is very wide, in order to deal with the change of ultrasonic frequency with the detection object. The hemispherical array sensor developed by piezoelectric material is used to image blood vessels, and the experimental results show that the transducer can obtain high imaging resolution.

articleTitle: In orbit pointing calibration scheme and performance simulation of multi-beam antenna
abstract: Multi-beam antennas generally adopt narrow beam coverage, frequency multiplexing and other technologies, which have high requirements for antenna pointing accuracy. For communication satellites in synchronous orbit, a scheme of in orbit pointing calibration of multi-beam antenna is proposed based on the principle of amplitude comparison monopulse. By comparing the amplitudes of the beacon signals, the antenna pointing measurement is realized, the compensation parameters are generated, and the antenna pointing control is realized by adjusting satellite attitude. Based on the analysis of pointing error source and calibration error, the accuracy of calibration is estimated, and the calibration performance is simulated.

articleTitle: Optimization of Chebyshev Low-pass Topology based Broadband Power Amplifier Using PSO Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, a broadband power amplifier (PA) is designed using particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The Chebyshev low-pass topology is employed to establish initial matching network of the PA. The matching impedance of the network is optimized by the PSO algorithm. The simulation results show that, with the proposed optimization method, excellent impedance matching network can be obtained. The power added efficiency (PAE) can be improved more than 10% averagely, which greater than 70%, and output power improved 1 dBm averagely, which arrived bigger than 41 dBm in the frequency band between 2GHz to 3GHz, which validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed design method.

articleTitle: Wideband Absorptive Common-Mode Filter Based on Hybrid Structures of Quarter-Wavelength Slot and Microstrip Resonators
abstract: This paper presents a novel wideband absorptive common-mode filter which is constructed by differential microstrip lines, two hybrid resonator unit-cells made of quarter-wavelength slot and microstrip structures, two lumped resistors, and a ground plane. Two resonator structures, including quar-ter-wavelength slot and microstrip lines, share the same resonant frequency at which the common-mode energy can be absorbed by lumped resistors.
