Furthermore, two resonator unit-cells are cascaded symmetrically beneath differential lines to realize bidi-rectional and wideband common-mode absorption. The measured results show that the proposed common-mode filter can exhibit low insertion loss for differential signals, and achieve a wide absorptive stopband from 1.55 to 2.65 GHz (Absorption ratio > 90%) with 52.38% fractional bandwidth simultaneously.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Metasurface with Polarization-Independent and Wide-Angle-Incident Performances for 2.45GHz and 5.8GHz
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band and polarization-independent metasurface with wide range of incident angle for harvesting ambient electromagnetic energy. The proposed unit structure consists of a centrosymmetric metal closed-ring cross, F4B substrate, and 4 loads connected to the ground through 4 metal vias. The fully centrosymmetric structure keeps the working performances of the proposed metasurface unchanged under different polarization directions. Simulation results show that more than 80% of the energy at 2.45GHz and 5.8GHz can be captured at any incident angle ranging from 0°to 60°, taking into account the slight offset of the resonant frequency (no more than 0.05GHz).

articleTitle: Phase Synchronization in Ultra Narrow Band Transmission With Orbital Angular Momentum Microwave
abstract: With the fast development of the internet, the requirements for communication quality continue to increase. Accordingly, spectrum resources become scarce. The Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) has been widely researched in recent years and can be used for communication. OAM is a physical quantity different from electric field strength. Quantum OAM reflects the new physical dimension of OAM. Using quantum OAM for communication, Ultra Narrow Band (UNB) transmission can be realized on the spectrum. In the UNB system with OAM, phase synchronization is the key part. This paper proposes a method to implement the UNB system with phase synchronization. The simulation results are given to verify the effectiveness.

articleTitle: Design of a 17-21 GHz Power Amplifier Based on an Extended Resistive Continuous Mode
abstract: In this paper, an efficiency improvement method in multistage power amplifier (PA) is proposed. Combined with the power stage transistor operate in continuous class-F and the driver stage transistor operate in continuous class-F-<sup>1</sup>, the power-added efficiency (PAE) of multistage PA can be further improved. Meanwhile, a large power push ratio is adopted to determine the size of transistors at each stage and a voltage divider circuit is used to maintain the same bias. The proposed method was verified by implementing an MMIC PA utilizing a 0.1 <tex>$\mu \text{mGaAs}$</tex> pHEMT process. The PA is used for the 17–21 GHz satellite communication system with a saturated output power of 1 W and an average PAE higher than 44% while having a small signal gain of 23 dB.

articleTitle: Circular Patch Resonator Loaded Compact SIW Filter with Harmonic Suppression
abstract: In this paper, based on a hybrid structure using the patch resonator and substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity, a compact bandpass filter (BPF) with a wide stopband is proposed. The patch resonator is connected with two SIW cavities by coplanar waveguide lines at both ends. It can not only extend the order of the proposed filter but also suppress the TE<inf>201</inf>and TE202 modes of the SIW cavity. In addition, the offset orthogonal ports can prevent the propagation of the <tex>$\mathbf{TE}_{102}$</tex> mode of the SIW cavities. Thus, a wide stopband is achieved by suppressing the first three spurious modes. For validation, a prototype was fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Sampling Criteria for 3-D Holographic Millimeter Wave Imaging
abstract: This paper presents more precise sampling criteria for 3-D holographic millimeter wave imaging. Firstly, spatial and frequency sampling criteria are derived according to the Nyquist sampling theorem. The sampling criteria are more precise since the imaging distance, the length of the synthesis antenna aperture, and the wavelength are taken into account. The sampling intervals of the spatial sampling are larger than <tex>$\lambda/4$</tex>. Hence, the results can provide guidance for the design of the antenna array for millimeter wave imaging system.

articleTitle: A High-Q Optically Transparent Millimeter-wave Absorber with Stable Angular Response
abstract: An optically transparent narrow-band millimeter-wave absorber with a high quality factor (Q), polarization insensi-tivity, wide incident angle stability, high absorptivity was demon-strated. The metamaterial absorber (MMA) is composed of poly-ethylene terephthalate (PET), metal grid structures, glass, and in-dium tin oxide (ITO), all of these materials own high optical transparency, resulting in the optically transparent property for the proposed absorber. The absorber achieves 6.5% fractional bandwidth for deep absorptivity (>90<sup>%</sup>) at a center frequency of 37.2 GHz. A high <tex>$Q$</tex> value (>5) is realized by tailoring the resistance of metal grid closed-ring resonators. Further analysis illustrated that the absorber maintains efficient absorption under wide inci-dent angles and polarizations, indicating potential applications in wireless communication fields.

articleTitle: Interference Emission Sources Identification Approach Based on Basic Emission Waveform Theory
abstract: With the rapid development of electronic technology in recent years, the application of electronic equipment or electronic system becomes more and more common, and these equipment or system produce a large number of intentional or unintentional electromagnetic emissions when they are working. In order to check the electromagnetic emission to avoid the impact on the surrounding electronic equipment or electronic system, the need of emitter identification arises, especially in the field of electromagnetic compatibility(EMC). This paper proposes a systematic radiation emitter identification approach. This approach divides the radiated emission data of equipment or system into three different kinds of components and the radiated emission data is classified according to the similarity of the three components. Three different kinds of electronic equipment radiation emission data are used to verify the proposed method. The classification accuracy for small samples of radiation emission data is 100%, which confirms the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Filtering Phase Shifters Using Vertically Installed Planar Structure
abstract: In this paper, a wideband filtering phase shifter (PS) is proposed using vertically installed circuit structures, where the VIP circuit is used to realize a tight coupling. The even-odd mode analysis is adopted to analyze the whole structure. Then, a 45° filtering PS is designed to verify the design methodology. The simulated and measured results demonstrate that the proposed phase shifter has low insertion losses (<0.5 dB) and excellent return losses (< -15 dB). The 3°-phase shift bandwidth is more than 64.31%.

articleTitle: Joint Modulation of Amplitude and Polarization for Metasurface-Based Wireless Communication System
abstract: In this paper, we propose a binary amplitude-shift keying (BASK) wireless communication system based on a metasurface capable of joint modulation of amplitude and polarization. By modulating the spatial profile of the metasurface meta-atoms, we obtain different cross-polarized reflections from the metasurface that can be further dynamically tuned. As the exemplary demonstration, transmitted information is successfully recovered at the receiving terminal. Our proposed system may have further envisions in polarimetry detecting and imaging.

articleTitle: Improved GHI - LFM Algorithm Based on Coherence Factor
abstract: In this paper, the recently indigenously developed millimeter-wave imaging (MMWI) algoritthm GHI-LFM, namely general holographic imaging (HI) algorithm based on linear frequency modulation (LFM), is further improved by using coherence factor (CF), called GHI-LFM-CF. The new method can suppress the Gibb's effect in k-space, resulting in very clean background. The superior performance is validated by imaging using both synthetic and experimental data of benchmark objects.

articleTitle: A Compact I/Q Network with Center-Tap Coupled Transformer-Based Quadrature Hybrids for Millimeter-Wave Applications
abstract: In this paper, a compact broadband in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) network is realized based on transformer-based quadrature hybrids. The coupling capacitors of the proposed hybrid locate at the center taps of the transformer. All output ports of the center-tap coupled quadrature hybrid locate at the same side of the transformer, which makes signal path and power routing much easier. Based on the center-tap coupled hybrid, the proposed I/Q network shows a good performance with less area. A lumped-element model of the center-tap coupled quadrature hybrid is also investigated. Based on the 40-nm CMOS process, an I/Q network with 2-stage transformer-based quadrature hybrids is implemented. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed structure achieves an image rejection ratio (IRR) of more than 35 dB from 17 GHz to 31 GHz. Furthermore, the area of the proposed structure is 392*379 um<sup>2</sup>.

articleTitle: High-isolation Millimeter-wave Wide-angle Scanning Phased Array U sing Overlapped Metasurface Structure
abstract: This manuscript presents a millimeter-wave phased array with the merits of high isolation, low active <tex>$\mathrm{S}$</tex> parameters and wide-angle scanning. Firstly, overlapped metasurface structure is proposed to construct a very miniaturized broadband antenna element with the size of only <tex>$0.17\lambda_{0}$</tex>. Then, the newly designed element is placed with a small distance of about <tex>$0.4\lambda_{0}$</tex> for implementing <tex>$1\times 4$</tex> wide-angle scanning phased array. Benefit from the small size of the elements, there are enough space to load decoupling structure for ensuring high isolation. The results show that the array can cover the 5G band from 24.25 to 29.5 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 19.53%, and the isolation between adjacent elements is basically higher than 20dB. Moreover, it can achieve a large scanning range of -61° ~61° in low band and -55°~55° in high band respectively, meanwhile, all the active S parameters can keep lower than -8.4dB for ensuring scanning efficiency. These results reveal that the proposed array would be potentially applied in 5G millimeter-wave communication.

articleTitle: A Tunable Band-pass FSS Structure for 5G Applications
abstract: A tunable band-pass FSS structure is proposed in this paper, where the varactors are attached to acquire the tunability, and the inductors are introduced to work as AC blocks. The results show that the passband can be tuned from 1.75GHz - 1.98GHz to 2.35GHz - 2.95GHz by changing the DC bias attaching to the varactor. And the structure shows good angular stability. The proposed tunable FSS structure is widely applied for electromagnetic interference shielding between the antennas in integrated antenna systems. The proposed structure shows the potential applications in 5G communication.

articleTitle: Contactless Detection for Heart Sounds Based on Doppler Radar Sensor
abstract: Heart sounds can provide crucial information regarding cardiovascular state. While the widely used heart sound detection methods always need complex signal processing and also require contact sensors. In this work, the feasibility of contactless detection of heart sounds based on Doppler radar sensor is demonstrated through experiments. A custom-designed 24G DC-coupled continuous-wave radar sensor, ECG device and PCG sensor were simultaneously employed to verify the arguments. The experimental results validated that the proposed technique has the potential to obtain the accurate heart sounds' timing information and waveform with low sampling rate (400 Hz) which provides a convenient way to detect heart sounds during daily life.

articleTitle: A highly integrated on-line monitoring system for RF applications
abstract: A highly integrated monitoring system based on the system in packaging (SIP) technology is investigated. The BGA packaged monitoring chip with dimensions of 1 cm <tex>$\times 1$</tex> cm is designed and fabricated successfully. The operation frequency of the system is 0.1-18 GHz and the advised detected power is ranged from -14 to 2 dBm. Experiments show that the approximate piecewise linear relationships between the output voltage change and the input RF power are obtained. Results also demonstrate that the sensitivity is calculated to be 0.04 dBm and the environmental adaptability from -50 °C to 70 °C is good, indicating that the monitoring system is suitable for almost all RF applications such as 5G communication radio, 5G-IOT, radar, and industrial microwave heating.

articleTitle: A Mapping-Based Three-Level Direct Digital Radio Frequency Modulation for All-Digital Transmitters
abstract: In this paper, a mapping-based 3-level direct digital radio frequency modulation (DDRFM) algorithm for alldigital transmitters (ADTx) is proposed and investigated, which offers the advantages of coding efficiency (CE), flexibility and configurability. It is shown that by adjusting the look-up table (LUT) with the requirements, multi-objective optimization and RF signals can be flexibly and effectively achieved. For realizing the direct mapping of modulation information and pulse waveform, the proposed approach uses DSM as the baseband modulation (BBM) and performs 3-level mapping pulse width modulation (3L-MPWM). Hence, the design complexity and memory issues are solved. Furthermore, the optimal key modulation parameters (KMP) under this scheme are analyzed and verified. The research results validate the reliability and effectiveness of the optimization model.

articleTitle: A V-band Differential Colpitts Push-Push VCO in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: A V-band push-push VCO operating from 68.5 GHz to 73 GHz is presented. This design introduces a capacitor at the common-base node, which enhances odd mode oscillation and maximizes the common-mode impedance of the differential oscillator. At the output end, a transformer is used to decouple both fundamental and 2<sup>nd</sup> harmonic frequency signals. The desired 2<sup>nd</sup> harmonic frequency signal is delivered to the output, whereas the fundamental frequency signal can be fed back for phase-detection in a phase-locked loop. The implemented VCO delivers a peak output power of 1.2 dBm at 72.5 GHz, and achieves a phase noise of -103 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset, respectively. The circuit is designed on a 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology with <tex>$f_{T}/f_{max}$</tex> of 200/300 GHz. The total power consumption of the signal source is 50 mW with a supply voltage of 1.8 V.

articleTitle: A Broadband Flip-Chip Microwave Amplifier on a LTCC Substrate
abstract: In this paper, a flip-chip vertical interconnect transition structure is designed based on the existing integration process, and a 2GHz∼6GHz amplifier chip is integrated on LTCC circuit with leadless interconnection by using the flip-chip vertical interconnect transition structure. The integrated circuit is simulated, fabricated and measured, the simulated and measured results show a good match. It is a good reference for application of high density integration microwave microsystems.

articleTitle: A Massive MIMO Channel Estimation Algorithm Design Combined the SVD Method with LS Signal Detection
abstract: In order to meet people's demand for communication rate, massive MIMO technology has been introduced into 5G field, which has become a research hotspot due to its advantages of improving system capacity, ensuring communication quality and reducing communication cost. The acquisition of channel state information (CSI) is the basis of massive MIMO, however, the accuracy of existing channel estimation techniques is difficult to reach a satisfactory standard, especially when the number of antennas is small. In order to correct the shortcomings, this paper introduces the idea of least square signal detection on the basis of the traditional singular value decomposition (SVD) channel estimation algorithm. The joint algorithm uses SVD algorithm to calculate the channel matrix as the initial value of the signal detection, and then re-estimate the channel state by using the detected signal and the transmitted pilot. The theory and simulation show that the proposed estimation algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy of the estimation results compared with the traditional channel estimation algorithm.

articleTitle: Generation of Broadband Dual Tilted Bessel Beams with Polarization Conversion Metasurface
abstract: In this paper, broadband dual tilted Bessel beams with the aid of a polarization conversion meta-surface is generated. The transmission meta-surface consists of 32*32 subwavelength unit cells, which can effectively convert incident linear polarized wave to zero order Bessel beam with different direction based on time reversal. The designed three-layer unit cell combining mirrored and size changed approach can meet the need of full 360° phase coverage from 10GHz to 18GHz with high transmission magnitude (>0.9). The developed dual Bessel beams propagate along the <tex>$\mathrm{e}=30^{\mathrm{o}}, \varphi=45^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> and <tex>$\Theta=-30_{J}\varphi=180^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex>.And their simulated magnitude distributions in near field are provided.

articleTitle: Compact Integrated Duplex Filtering Antenna with Common Feeding and Radiating SIW Cavities
abstract: In this paper, a compact integrated duplex filtering antenna is proposed based on co-shared substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity. Firstly, a dual-mode TE<inf>102</inf> and (TE<inf>201</inf> modes) rectangular cavity with two input ports is utilized as a common feeding cavity to respectively contribute one transmission poles for each channel. And then, an additional square cavity with a rectangular ring slot is coupled from the lower feeding cavity for both dual-mode excitation and duplexing passband radiation. To verify the proposed concept, a prototype duplex filtering antenna is simulated. The duplex filtering antenna resonates at 7.27 GHz and 8.06 GHz with a low cross-polarization and a high gain of 5.82 dBi and 6.91 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Contactless Detection of Mouse's Licking with a 120 GHz Interferometric Radar
abstract: Accurate quantification of behavior has positive in-fluence on the understanding of brain. It is important to monitor movement behaviors for subjects like human and animals. In this paper, a contactless technique for detecting mouse's licking using a custom-designed 120 GHz millimeter-wave radar sensing system is proposed. The experimental scene to test the cognitive judg-ments of mouse is also given. Owing to the miniaturized size, the radar sensor could be placed on the water needle and close to the tongue of mouse without blocking the mouse's sight in a virtual space. The system has been validated and the experimental results show that the movement situations of mouse could be distin-guished precisely based on the proposed technique, such as licking, running on the scroll wheel and touching needle with paws. The detection technique of the behavioral state of mouse lays the groundwork for the study of subsequent association of animal movement and perception.

articleTitle: Novel Miniature evanescent mode filter for wideband spurious suppression
abstract: In this paper, a novel method is proposed to design a high-order harmonic suppression filter. By improving the original coaxial cavity filter structure, the two modes of the resonant cavity can be separated and loading evanescent modes waveguide to prevent higher-order mode propagation. It can suppress high-order harmonics while meeting the requirements of low-frequency suppression, and the filter has a compact structure and is convenient for cascading. The simulation results show that the center frequency of the filter is 2.3GHz, the bandwidth is 300MHz, the suppression is higher than 40dB in dc to 1.8GHz, and the upper stopband can have an attenuation level near 40 dB up to more than 15 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a 3.5GHz Dual-polarized Curved Phased Array for 3D Coverage Communication
abstract: In this paper, a 3.5GHz dual-polarized curved phased array is presented. This array comprises five 1 x8 units sub-arrays and has 80 channels in total. The calculation method about the feed phase for beam scanning to the units has been given. The array can achieve beam scanning from 30° to 110° in the pitch range, with a maximum transmit beam gain of 46.5dBi and 46.7 dBi. It can be used as one part of ground base station for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) air-to-ground communication to built a 3-dimension (3D) coverage communication network.

articleTitle: A Wideband E-plane Vertical Transition from Rectangle Waveguide to Groove Gap Waveguide
abstract: Gap waveguide (GW) technology solves the electrical contact problem through a contactless way and makes the packaging of multilayer millimeter wave systems much easier. In this work, a wideband E-plane vertical transition from hollow rectangle waveguide (RW) to groove gap waveguide (GGW) for multilayer millimeter-wave packaged system is proposed. An inverted bended stepped structure is designed for wideband impedance matching between the vertical RW and the horizontal GGW. An air gap exists between the bended steps and the cover of GGW to maintain the advantage of contactless. To avoid resonation between the bended steps and the top cover plate, the width of the bended steps is narrowed and a rectangular region is cut off to reduce the surface of the bended steps further. A Ka-band prototype of the transition is designed, fabricated and tested, over the entire Ka-band, the measured insertion loss is less than 0.15dB, and the return loss is better than 20dB.

articleTitle: Microstrip-Ridge Gap Waveguide Layer Transition for Compact Wave-guide Packaging Interconnection
abstract: For millimeter-wave integrated circuit packaging and interconnection application, a microstrip-ridge gap wave-guide (MRGW) layer transition structure is proposed. MRGW consists of an array of mushroom units and the microstrip line which is shorted to the ground plane. Above the layer of MRGW, there is the layer transition, including a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) resonant cavity and the tapered microstrip line, which is composed to achieve impedance matching and the field coupling between the MRGW and the microstrip line. Full-wave simulation software is used to design and simulate the back-to-back layer transition. The numerical simulation results indicates that the proposed transition operates at 64.8-76.5GHz, with the return loss <tex>$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert$</tex> higher than 15 dB.

articleTitle: A High-Order-Mode OAM Patch Antenna with High Gain and Low Divergence
abstract: A high-order-mode two-feed orbital angular momentum (OAM) patch antenna at Ka-band is proposed in this paper. The circularly polarized OAM patch antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 23.7% with more than 10-dB return loss. A vortex beam carrying <tex>$l=\pm 1$</tex> OAM mode is generated with a mode purity over 85% from 26.5 GHz to 33 GHz. Additionally, by loading a low-profile lens, the maximum gain can be improved from 6.7 dBic to 15.7 dBic, and the beam divergence angle converges from 37° to 6°.
